name: Maryland

statute.name: Maryland Public Information Act (PIA)
statute.citation: Md. Code Ann., Gen. Prov. §§ 4-101 to 4-601 (response § 4-203)

response.rule_text: Custodian must grant or deny within 30 days of the application (act immediately when access is clear); a denial notice with reasons is due within 10 working days; the period may be extended up to 30 more days only with applicant consent, Gen. Prov. § 4-203.

fees.labor_rule: Reasonable fee for actual costs of search, preparation and production, but no charge for the first two hours, Gen. Prov. § 4-206.
fees.waiver_rule: Custodian may waive fees if applicant is indigent (affidavit) or on request after considering ability to pay and public benefit, § 4-206(e).

appeal.body: Public Access Ombudsman (mediation), then PIA Compliance Board; or circuit court
appeal.rule_text: Since July 2022 requesters must first mediate with the Public Access Ombudsman (GP § 4-1B-04), then may complain to the PIA Compliance Board (binding orders, § 4-1A-04) within 30 days from the ombudsman's final determination (§ 4-1A-05(b)(5)); judicial review (§ 4-362) needs no prior administrative step.

notes: Deadline to request Ombudsman mediation is not set by statute. Compliance Board fee jurisdiction limited to fees over $350. School districts included in 'political subdivision' (§ 4-101). Governor case (Office of Governor v. Washington Post) cited but coverage rule not extracted. Silence-is-denial not found. Appeal deadline null: the 30 days runs from the ombudsman's final determination, not from the denial.
